objects.definition:
typedef struct TagunzFile__ { int unused; } unzFile__;
typedef unzFile__ *unzFile;
objects.description: Opaque handle type for an open ZIP archive when STRICTUNZIP/STRICTZIPUNZIP is defined. Represents a ZIP file instance managed by the MiniZip unzip API. When STRICT is not defined, unzFile is a void pointer; in that case this strict typed alias may not be present. Creation is via unzOpen* functions and it is closed with unzClose. Do not dereference; contents are private.
Timestamp structure used by MiniZip to report file date/time in archives, similar to struct tm but restricted to DOS date ranges.
Holds global ZIP archive metadata for Zip64, including total entry count (64-bit) and global comment size. Filled by unzGetGlobalInfo64.
Holds global ZIP archive metadata (32-bit entry count) and global comment size. Filled by unzGetGlobalInfo.

objects.definition:
typedef struct unz_file_info64_s
{
    uLong version;              /* version made by                 2 bytes */
    uLong version_needed;       /* version needed to extract       2 bytes */
    uLong flag;                 /* general purpose bit flag        2 bytes */
    uLong compression_method;   /* compression method              2 bytes */
    uLong dosDate;              /* last mod file date in Dos fmt   4 bytes */
    uLong crc;                  /* crc-32                          4 bytes */
    ZPOS64_T compressed_size;   /* compressed size                 8 bytes */
    ZPOS64_T uncompressed_size; /* uncompressed size               8 bytes */
    uLong size_filename;        /* filename length                 2 bytes */
    uLong size_file_extra;      /* extra field length              2 bytes */
    uLong size_file_comment;    /* file comment length             2 bytes */

    uLong disk_num_start;       /* disk number start               2 bytes */
    uLong internal_fa;          /* internal file attributes        2 bytes */
    uLong external_fa;          /* external file attributes        4 bytes */

    tm_unz tmu_date;
} unz_file_info64;
objects.description: Per-entry metadata for a file in a Zip64 archive, including method, CRC, sizes, attributes, and timestamp. Filled by unzGetCurrentFileInfo64.

objects.definition:

    uLong dosDate;              /* last mod file date in Dos fmt   4 bytes */

    tm_unz tmu_date;

objects.description: Per-entry metadata for a file in a ZIP archive (32-bit sizes). Filled by unzGetCurrentFileInfo.
Position descriptor for locating a file inside the central directory using 32-bit offsets. Used with unzGetFilePos and unzGoToFilePos.
Zip64-capable position descriptor for locating a file inside the central directory using 64-bit offsets. Used with unzGetFilePos64 and unzGoToFilePos64.

objects.definition: typedef voidpf   (ZCALLBACK *open_file_func)      OF((voidpf opaque, const TCHAR* filename, int mode));
objects.description: Function pointer type for opening a file/stream in the 32-bit filefunc API. Implementations are supplied when customizing IO backends.

objects.definition: typedef uLong    (ZCALLBACK *read_file_func)      OF((voidpf opaque, voidpf stream, void* buf, uLong size));
objects.description: Function pointer type for reading from a stream in the filefunc API.

objects.description: Function pointer type for writing to a stream in the filefunc API.

objects.definition: typedef int      (ZCALLBACK *close_file_func)     OF((voidpf opaque, voidpf stream));
objects.description: Function pointer type for closing a stream in the filefunc API.

objects.definition: typedef int      (ZCALLBACK *testerror_file_func) OF((voidpf opaque, voidpf stream));
objects.description: Function pointer type to test error status for a stream in the filefunc API.

objects.definition: typedef long     (ZCALLBACK *tell_file_func)      OF((voidpf opaque, voidpf stream));
objects.description: Function pointer type returning 32-bit tell/position for a stream.

Aggregates 32-bit file operation callbacks used to plug custom IO backends into MiniZip.

objects.definition: typedef ZPOS64_T (ZCALLBACK *tell64_file_func)    OF((voidpf opaque, voidpf stream));
objects.description: Function pointer type returning 64-bit tell/position for a stream.

Aggregates 64-bit file operation callbacks used to plug custom IO backends and support large files in MiniZip.
Bridging structure combining 64-bit callbacks with optional 32-bit open/tell/seek for compatibility. Used internally to call appropriate functions via wrappers.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned long long int ZPOS64_T;
objects.description: Unsigned 64-bit file position/size type used throughout MiniZip for Zip64 support. Actual typedef may vary by platform/defines; here it resolves to 64-bit unsigned integer if no custom type is provided.

functions.name: unzStringFileNameCompare
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzStringFileNameCompare(const char* fileName1, const char* fileName2, int iCaseSensitivity);
functions.description: Compares two ZIP entry filenames with configurable case sensitivity. Use to match or sort names when browsing a ZIP archive.
requirements: fileName1 must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
fileName2 must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
iCaseSensitivity: 1 = case-sensitive (strcmp-like), 2 = case-insensitive (strcasecmp-like), 0 = OS default (case-sensitive on Unix, case-insensitive on Windows).

functions.name: unzOpen
functions.signature: unzFile ZEXPORT unzOpen(const TCHAR *path);
functions.description: Opens a ZIP file for reading using the default file API. Returns an unzFile handle on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: path must point to a valid, null-terminated path to a ZIP file.
The returned unzFile must be closed with unzClose.
If the file cannot be opened or is not a valid ZIP, NULL is returned and must be checked before further calls.

functions.name: unzOpen64
functions.signature: unzFile ZEXPORT unzOpen64(const void *path);
functions.description: Opens a ZIP file for reading (Zip64-capable). The path is passed through to the provided 64-bit filefunc open callback. Returns an unzFile or NULL on failure.
requirements: path must be the same type expected by the configured open64_file_func (e.g., wide string on Windows when using fill_fopen64_filefunc).
Check for NULL on failure before using the returned handle.
Close the handle with unzClose when done.

functions.name: unzOpen2
functions.signature: unzFile ZEXPORT unzOpen2(const TCHAR *path, zlib_filefunc_def* pzlib_filefunc_def);
functions.description: Opens a ZIP file using a caller-provided 32-bit file function table (ioapi.h). Allows custom I/O backends.
requirements: path must be a valid, null-terminated path representation compatible with the provided filefuncs.
pzlib_filefunc_def must point to a fully initialized zlib_filefunc_def structure.
On failure returns NULL; callers must check for NULL before use.
Close the returned handle with unzClose.

functions.name: unzOpen2_64
functions.signature: unzFile ZEXPORT unzOpen2_64(const void *path, zlib_filefunc64_def* pzlib_filefunc_def);
functions.description: Opens a ZIP file using a caller-provided 64-bit file function table (ioapi.h). Supports large files and custom backends.
requirements: path must be the same type expected by the provided open64_file_func (opaque const void*).
pzlib_filefunc_def must point to a fully initialized zlib_filefunc64_def structure.
Returns NULL on failure and must be checked before use.
Close the returned handle with unzClose.

functions.name: unzClose
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzClose(unzFile file);
functions.description: Closes a ZIP handle previously opened by unzOpen/unzOpen64/unzOpen2/unzOpen2_64.
requirements: file must be a valid unzFile returned by an open function and not already closed.
All files opened with unzOpenCurrentFile/… must be closed with unzCloseCurrentFile before calling unzClose.

functions.name: unzGetGlobalInfo
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzGetGlobalInfo(unzFile file, unz_global_info *pglobal_info);
functions.description: Retrieves global ZIP information (entry count, comment size) into a 32-bit info struct.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile.
pglobal_info must be a valid pointer to unz_global_info; no pre-initialization required.
Returns UNZ_OK on success; caller should check the return code.

functions.name: unzGetGlobalInfo64
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzGetGlobalInfo64(unzFile file, unz_global_info64 *pglobal_info);
functions.description: Retrieves global ZIP information into a 64-bit capable info struct.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile.
pglobal_info must be a valid pointer to unz_global_info64; no pre-initialization required.
Returns UNZ_OK on success; caller should check the return code.

functions.name: unzGetGlobalComment
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzGetGlobalComment(unzFile file, char *szComment, uLong uSizeBuf);
functions.description: Copies the ZIP archive's global comment into the provided buffer.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile.
szComment must point to a buffer of at least uSizeBuf bytes when not NULL.
uSizeBuf is the size of szComment in bytes; can be 0 to query behavior (will return 0 copied).
Function returns number of bytes copied or a negative error code; caller must handle return value.

functions.name: unzGoToFirstFile
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzGoToFirstFile(unzFile file);
functions.description: Positions the directory cursor to the first file entry in the ZIP.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile.
Returns UNZ_OK on success; caller should check for errors.

functions.name: unzGoToNextFile
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzGoToNextFile(unzFile file);
functions.description: Advances the directory cursor to the next file entry in the ZIP.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile.
On end of list returns UNZ_END_OF_LIST_OF_FILE; caller must handle this sentinel.
Returns UNZ_OK on success; negative on error.

functions.name: unzLocateFile
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzLocateFile(unzFile file, const char *szFileName, int iCaseSensitivity);
functions.description: Searches for a file by name and, if found, makes it the current file.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile.
szFileName must be a valid, null-terminated C string; matching uses iCaseSensitivity per unzStringFileNameCompare semantics.
Returns UNZ_OK if found, UNZ_END_OF_LIST_OF_FILE if not found; caller must handle return value.

functions.name: unzGetFilePos
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzGetFilePos(unzFile file, unz_file_pos* file_pos);
functions.description: Retrieves a 32-bit file position descriptor for the current directory entry, usable to return later via unzGoToFilePos.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with a current file selected.
file_pos must be a valid pointer to unz_file_pos to receive the position.

functions.name: unzGoToFilePos
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzGoToFilePos(unzFile file, unz_file_pos* file_pos);
functions.description: Jumps to a previously saved 32-bit directory position, restoring the current file to that entry.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile.
file_pos must point to a position previously obtained via unzGetFilePos for the same archive.

functions.name: unzGetFilePos64
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzGetFilePos64(unzFile file, unz64_file_pos* file_pos);
functions.description: Retrieves a 64-bit file position descriptor for the current directory entry, for archives with large central directories.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with a current file selected.
file_pos must be a valid pointer to unz64_file_pos to receive the position.

functions.name: unzGoToFilePos64
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzGoToFilePos64(unzFile file, const unz64_file_pos* file_pos);
functions.description: Jumps to a previously saved 64-bit directory position, restoring the current file.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile.
file_pos must point to a position previously obtained via unzGetFilePos64 for the same archive.

functions.name: unzGetCurrentFileInfo64
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzGetCurrentFileInfo64(unzFile file, unz_file_info64 *pfile_info, char *szFileName, uLong fileNameBufferSize, void *extraField, uLong extraFieldBufferSize, char *szComment, uLong commentBufferSize);
functions.description: Retrieves metadata for the current file entry (Zip64-capable). Optionally returns the filename, central extra field, and comment into caller-provided buffers.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with a current file selected.
pfile_info may be NULL; if non-NULL must point to writable unz_file_info64.
szFileName may be NULL; if non-NULL, fileNameBufferSize is the capacity and must be sufficient to hold the name (including terminator as applicable).
extraField may be NULL; if non-NULL, extraFieldBufferSize is its capacity; copies the central-header version of the extra field.
szComment may be NULL; if non-NULL, commentBufferSize is its capacity.
Caller must check return code for success (UNZ_OK) or errors.

functions.name: unzGetCurrentFileInfo
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzGetCurrentFileInfo(unzFile file, unz_file_info *pfile_info, char *szFileName, uLong fileNameBufferSize, void *extraField, uLong extraFieldBufferSize, char *szComment, uLong commentBufferSize);
functions.description: Retrieves metadata for the current file entry (32-bit sizes). Optionally returns filename, central extra field, and comment.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with a current file selected.
pfile_info may be NULL; if non-NULL must point to writable unz_file_info.
szFileName may be NULL; if non-NULL, fileNameBufferSize must be the buffer capacity.
extraField may be NULL; if non-NULL, extraFieldBufferSize is its capacity; copies the central-header version of the extra field.
szComment may be NULL; if non-NULL, commentBufferSize is its capacity.
Caller must check the return code.

functions.name: unzGetCurrentFileZStreamPos64
functions.signature: ZPOS64_T ZEXPORT unzGetCurrentFileZStreamPos64(unzFile file);
functions.description: Returns the current file's zlib stream position as a 64-bit value (GDAL addition). Useful for advanced stream handling/debugging.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with a current file selected.

functions.name: unzOpenCurrentFile
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzOpenCurrentFile(unzFile file);
functions.description: Opens the current file entry for reading and decompression using default settings.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile and positioned on a file entry (via unzGoTo*/unzLocateFile).
Returns UNZ_OK on success; caller must check before reading.

functions.name: unzOpenCurrentFilePassword
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzOpenCurrentFilePassword(unzFile file, const char* password);
functions.description: Opens the current file entry for reading with the provided decryption password.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile positioned on a file entry.
password must be a valid, null-terminated string when required by the entry.
Returns UNZ_OK on success; caller must check before reading.

functions.name: unzOpenCurrentFile2
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzOpenCurrentFile2(unzFile file, int* method, int* level, int raw);
functions.description: Opens the current file entry for reading, optionally in raw mode (no decompression). Returns the compression method and level if requested.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile positioned on a file entry.
If method is non-NULL, it will receive the compression method; method cannot be NULL per comments.
level may be NULL; if non-NULL it will receive the compression level.
raw controls mode: 1 = raw (no decompression), 0 = normal decompression.
Returns UNZ_OK on success; caller must check.

functions.name: unzOpenCurrentFile3
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzOpenCurrentFile3(unzFile file, int* method, int* level, int raw, const char* password);
functions.description: Opens the current file entry for reading, optionally in raw mode, and optionally with a decryption password. Returns compression method and level if requested.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile positioned on a file entry.
method cannot be NULL per comments; it will receive the compression method.
level may be NULL; if non-NULL it will receive the compression level.
raw controls mode: 1 = raw (no decompression), 0 = normal decompression.
password may be NULL for unencrypted entries; if non-NULL must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Returns UNZ_OK on success; caller must check.

functions.name: unzCloseCurrentFile
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzCloseCurrentFile(unzFile file);
functions.description: Closes the current file entry opened with unzOpenCurrentFile/… and finalizes CRC verification.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with a current file entry previously opened for reading.
If the entire file was read and CRC does not match, returns UNZ_CRCERROR; caller must handle this error code before proceeding.

functions.name: unzReadCurrentFile
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzReadCurrentFile(unzFile file, voidp buf, unsigned len);
functions.description: Reads up to len bytes from the currently opened file entry into buf. Returns bytes read, 0 on EOF, or a negative error code.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with a file entry opened via unzOpenCurrentFile/…
buf must point to a writable memory region of at least len bytes.
len specifies the maximum number of bytes to read.
Caller must handle return values: >0 bytes read, 0 EOF, <0 error (UNZ_ERRNO for I/O or zlib error for decompression).

functions.name: unztell
functions.signature: z_off_t ZEXPORT unztell(unzFile file);
functions.description: Returns the current read position in the uncompressed data for the opened file entry (32-bit offset).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with a file entry opened for reading.

functions.name: unztell64
functions.signature: ZPOS64_T ZEXPORT unztell64(unzFile file);
functions.description: Returns the current read position in the uncompressed data for the opened file entry (64-bit offset).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with a file entry opened for reading.

functions.name: unzeof
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzeof(unzFile file);
functions.description: Checks whether end-of-file has been reached on the currently opened file entry. Returns 1 at EOF, 0 otherwise.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with a file entry opened for reading.

functions.name: unzGetLocalExtrafield
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzGetLocalExtrafield(unzFile file, voidp buf, unsigned len);
functions.description: Reads the local-header version of the extra field for the current file entry. If buf is NULL, returns the size of the local extra field; otherwise copies up to len bytes into buf.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with a current file selected (and typically opened).
If buf is non-NULL, it must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
Caller must check the return value: number of bytes copied (>=0) or negative error code.

functions.name: unzGetOffset64
functions.signature: ZPOS64_T ZEXPORT unzGetOffset64(unzFile file);
functions.description: Returns the current file offset within the ZIP central directory (64-bit). Useful for saving/restoring iteration state.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile.

functions.name: unzGetOffset
functions.signature: uLong ZEXPORT unzGetOffset(unzFile file);
functions.description: Returns the current file offset within the ZIP central directory (32-bit).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile.

functions.name: unzSetOffset64
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzSetOffset64(unzFile file, ZPOS64_T pos);
functions.description: Sets the current file offset within the ZIP central directory (64-bit), typically to a value previously obtained from unzGetOffset64.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile.
pos should be an offset previously obtained from unzGetOffset64 for the same archive to ensure validity.

functions.name: unzSetOffset
functions.signature: int ZEXPORT unzSetOffset(unzFile file, uLong pos);
functions.description: Sets the current file offset within the ZIP central directory (32-bit), typically to a value previously obtained from unzGetOffset.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile.
pos should be an offset previously obtained from unzGetOffset for the same archive to ensure validity.

functions.name: fill_fopen64_filefunc
functions.signature: void fill_fopen64_filefunc(zlib_filefunc64_def* pzlib_filefunc_def);
functions.description: Initializes a zlib_filefunc64_def with standard C file I/O functions (64-bit capable), suitable for use with unzOpen2_64/zip APIs.
requirements: pzlib_filefunc_def must be a non-NULL pointer to writable zlib_filefunc64_def.

functions.name: fill_fopen_filefunc
functions.signature: void fill_fopen_filefunc(zlib_filefunc_def* pzlib_filefunc_def);
functions.description: Initializes a zlib_filefunc_def with standard C file I/O functions (32-bit), suitable for use with unzOpen2/zip APIs.
requirements: pzlib_filefunc_def must be a non-NULL pointer to writable zlib_filefunc_def.

functions.name: call_zopen64
functions.signature: voidpf call_zopen64(const zlib_filefunc64_32_def* pfilefunc, const void* filename, int mode);
functions.description: Helper that invokes the open64 callback from a zlib_filefunc64_32_def to open a stream for the given filename and mode.
requirements: pfilefunc must be a non-NULL pointer to a fully initialized zlib_filefunc64_32_def.
filename must be a pointer compatible with the configured open function (opaque const void*).
mode must be a valid combination of ZLIB_FILEFUNC_MODE_* flags as expected by the backend.

functions.name: call_zseek64
functions.signature: long call_zseek64(const zlib_filefunc64_32_def* pfilefunc, voidpf filestream, ZPOS64_T offset, int origin);
functions.description: Helper that invokes the seek64 callback in a zlib_filefunc64_32_def to reposition the stream to offset relative to origin.
requirements: pfilefunc must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized zlib_filefunc64_32_def.
filestream must be a valid stream handle returned by the corresponding open function.
origin must be one of ZLIB_FILEFUNC_SEEK_SET, ZLIB_FILEFUNC_SEEK_CUR, or ZLIB_FILEFUNC_SEEK_END.
offset is a 64-bit position to seek to; backend must support it.

functions.name: call_ztell64
functions.signature: ZPOS64_T call_ztell64(const zlib_filefunc64_32_def* pfilefunc, voidpf filestream);
functions.description: Helper that invokes the tell64 callback in a zlib_filefunc64_32_def to obtain the current 64-bit position of the stream.
requirements: pfilefunc must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized zlib_filefunc64_32_def.
filestream must be a valid stream handle returned by the corresponding open function.

functions.name: fill_zlib_filefunc64_32_def_from_filefunc32
functions.signature: void fill_zlib_filefunc64_32_def_from_filefunc32(zlib_filefunc64_32_def* p_filefunc64_32, const zlib_filefunc_def* p_filefunc32);
functions.description: Builds a zlib_filefunc64_32_def wrapper from a provided 32-bit zlib_filefunc_def, enabling 64-bit compatible calls through adapters.
requirements: p_filefunc64_32 must be a non-NULL pointer to writable zlib_filefunc64_32_def.
p_filefunc32 must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized zlib_filefunc_def.

data_types.description: A generic null-terminated C string with no specific format constraints. May contain any bytes except the terminating NUL when passed via c_str(). Used for filenames, passwords, or general text comparisons.

A file whose contents follow the ZIP archive format, including a valid end of central directory and central directory records; may also be Zip64. The filename provided points to a file containing ZIP-formatted data.

A pointer value passed to file I/O callbacks expecting an opaque filename/identifier (const void*). In typical configurations this is a pointer to a null-terminated C string path, but the actual type is backend-defined. The data referenced identifies a file to open; the content of the referenced file is not interpreted at this stage.

import io
import random
import struct
import time
from typing import List, Tuple

# ZIP constants
# Signatures
LOCAL_FILE_HEADER_SIG = 0x04034B50
DATA_DESCRIPTOR_SIG = 0x08074B50
CENTRAL_DIR_HEADER_SIG = 0x02014B50
END_CENTRAL_DIR_SIG = 0x06054B50
ZIP64_END_CENTRAL_DIR_SIG = 0x06064B50
ZIP64_END_CENTRAL_DIR_LOC_SIG = 0x07064B50

# Compression methods
STORE = 0  # no compression
DEFLATE = 8  # deflate

# General purpose bit flags
GPF_ENCRYPTED = 0x0001
GPF_DATA_DESCRIPTOR = 0x0008
GPF_UTF8 = 0x0800

# Version needed
VER_NEEDED_DEFAULT = 20  # 2.0
VER_NEEDED_ZIP64 = 45    # 4.5 for ZIP64


def _dos_time_from_epoch(ts: float) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    # Convert to DOS date/time fields
    lt = time.localtime(ts)
    year = max(1980, min(2107, lt.tm_year))
    dos_date = ((year - 1980) << 9) | ((lt.tm_mon) << 5) | lt.tm_mday
    dos_time = (lt.tm_hour << 11) | (lt.tm_min << 5) | (lt.tm_sec // 2)
    return dos_date, dos_time


def _crc32(data: bytes) -> int:
    import zlib
    return zlib.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def _deflate(data: bytes, level: int = 6) -> bytes:
    import zlib
    comp = zlib.compressobj(level, zlib.DEFLATED, -15)  # raw deflate stream
    out = comp.compress(data) + comp.flush()
    return out


def _rand_filename(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a mix of names, directories, UTF-8
    choices = [
        "README.txt",
        "doc/guide.txt",
        "bin/exec",
        "data.bin",
        "unicodé/路径/文件.txt",
        "nested/dir/with/spaces/file name.txt",
        "empty/",
        "image.png",
        "config.ini",
        "a" * rnd.randint(1, 40) + ("/" if rnd.random() < 0.2 else "")
    ]
    return rnd.choice(choices)


def _make_extra_zip64(rnd: random.Random, uncompressed: int, compressed: int, header_offset: int) -> bytes:
    # ZIP64 extra field header id 0x0001
    # content can include sizes and offset if any exceed 0xFFFFFFFF
    fields = []
    if uncompressed >= 0xFFFFFFFF:
        fields.append(struct.pack("<Q", uncompressed))
    if compressed >= 0xFFFFFFFF:
        fields.append(struct.pack("<Q", compressed))
    if header_offset >= 0xFFFFFFFF:
        fields.append(struct.pack("<Q", header_offset))
    data = b"".join(fields)
    return struct.pack("<HH", 0x0001, len(data)) + data


def _central_extra_padding(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Include some common extra fields like NTFS times or UNIX UID/GID optionally
    parts = []
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        # Extended timestamp (0x5455)
        # Flags: 0x07 (mod, access, create), then three 4-byte unix times
        now = int(time.time())
        payload = struct.pack("<BIII", 0x07, now, now, now)
        parts.append(struct.pack("<HH", 0x5455, len(payload)) + payload)
    if rnd.random() < 0.25:
        # UNIX UID/GID (0x7875 Info-ZIP Unix Extra Field ("ux"))
        uid = rnd.randint(0, 65535)
        gid = rnd.randint(0, 65535)
        body = struct.pack("<BBHBBH", 1, 4, uid, 1, 4, gid)
        parts.append(struct.pack("<HH", 0x7875, len(body)) + body)
    return b"".join(parts)


def _build_file_entry(rnd: random.Random, name: str, content: bytes, method: int, use_descriptor: bool,
                      force_zip64_sizes: bool, utf8: bool, cur_offset: int) -> Tuple[bytes, dict]:
    # Prepare fields
    crc = _crc32(content)
    if method == STORE:
        comp = content
    elif method == DEFLATE:
        comp = _deflate(content, rnd.choice([0, 6, 9]))
    else:
        comp = content
    comp_size = len(comp)
    uncomp_size = len(content)

    gp_flag = 0
    if use_descriptor:
        gp_flag |= GPF_DATA_DESCRIPTOR
    if utf8:
        gp_flag |= GPF_UTF8

    dos_date, dos_time = _dos_time_from_epoch(time.time())

    # For local header, when data descriptor is used, set sizes and crc to 0 in header.
    lh_crc = 0 if use_descriptor else crc
    lh_csize = 0 if use_descriptor else comp_size
    lh_usize = 0 if use_descriptor else uncomp_size

    name_bytes = name.encode('utf-8')

    # Local extra: we typically don't include ZIP64 here unless needed by spec with descriptor; keep simple
    local_extra = b""

    local_header = struct.pack(
        "<IHHHHHIIIHH",
        LOCAL_FILE_HEADER_SIG,
        VER_NEEDED_ZIP64 if force_zip64_sizes else VER_NEEDED_DEFAULT,
        gp_flag,
        method,
        dos_time,
        dos_date,
        lh_crc,
        lh_csize,
        lh_usize,
        len(name_bytes),
        len(local_extra)
    ) + name_bytes + local_extra

    data = local_header + comp

    if use_descriptor:
        # Write data descriptor with signature
        data += struct.pack("<I", DATA_DESCRIPTOR_SIG)
        # If ZIP64 sizes are forced, use 8-byte sizes in descriptor per APPNOTE
        if force_zip64_sizes or comp_size >= 0xFFFFFFFF or uncomp_size >= 0xFFFFFFFF:
            data += struct.pack("<IQQ", crc, comp_size, uncomp_size)
        else:
            data += struct.pack("<III", crc, comp_size, uncomp_size)

    # Central directory header for this file
    made_by = 0x031E  # pretend UNIX 3.0+ (arbitrary)

    cen_ver_needed = VER_NEEDED_ZIP64 if (force_zip64_sizes or comp_size >= 0xFFFFFFFF or uncomp_size >= 0xFFFFFFFF or cur_offset >= 0xFFFFFFFF) else VER_NEEDED_DEFAULT

    # ZIP64 extra field if any 32-bit overflow or we force
    zip64_extra = _make_extra_zip64(rnd,
                                    0xFFFFFFFF if (force_zip64_sizes or uncomp_size >= 0xFFFFFFFF) else 0,
                                    0xFFFFFFFF if (force_zip64_sizes or comp_size >= 0xFFFFFFFF) else 0,
                                    0xFFFFFFFF if (force_zip64_sizes or cur_offset >= 0xFFFFFFFF) else 0)
    # The above helper packs only values present; if we fed 0, it will not include them. Fix logic:
    zip64_fields = []
    add_usize = force_zip64_sizes or uncomp_size >= 0xFFFFFFFF
    add_csize = force_zip64_sizes or comp_size >= 0xFFFFFFFF
    add_ofs = force_zip64_sizes or cur_offset >= 0xFFFFFFFF
    if add_usize:
        zip64_fields.append(struct.pack("<Q", uncomp_size))
    if add_csize:
        zip64_fields.append(struct.pack("<Q", comp_size))
    if add_ofs:
        zip64_fields.append(struct.pack("<Q", cur_offset))
    if zip64_fields:
        zip64_extra = struct.pack("<HH", 0x0001, 8 * len(zip64_fields)) + b"".join(zip64_fields)
    else:
        zip64_extra = b""

    central_extra = zip64_extra + _central_extra_padding(rnd)

    ext_attr = 0o100644 << 16  # regular file perms in upper 2 bytes
    if name.endswith('/'):
        ext_attr = 0o040755 << 16  # directory

    rel_offset = cur_offset

    cen = struct.pack(
        "<IHHHHHHIIIHHHHHII",
        CENTRAL_DIR_HEADER_SIG,
        made_by,
        cen_ver_needed,
        gp_flag,
        method,
        dos_time,
        dos_date,
        crc,
        comp_size if not (add_csize) else 0xFFFFFFFF,
        uncomp_size if not (add_usize) else 0xFFFFFFFF,
        len(name_bytes),
        len(central_extra),
        0,  # file comment length
        0,  # disk number start
        0,  # internal attrs
        ext_attr,
        rel_offset if not add_ofs else 0xFFFFFFFF,
    ) + name_bytes + central_extra

    info = {
        "is_dir": name.endswith('/'),
        "crc": crc,
        "comp_size": comp_size,
        "uncomp_size": uncomp_size,
        "gp_flag": gp_flag,
        "method": method,
        "offset": rel_offset,
        "name": name,
        "zip64": bool(zip64_extra),
    }
    return data, {"central": cen, "info": info}


def _build_archive(rnd: random.Random, files: List[Tuple[str, bytes, int, bool, bool, bool]]) -> bytes:
    # files: list of tuples (name, content, method, use_descriptor, force_zip64_sizes, utf8)
    chunks = []
    centrals = []
    offset = 0
    for name, content, method, use_desc, force_zip64, utf8 in files:
        entry_data, cen = _build_file_entry(rnd, name, content, method, use_desc, force_zip64, utf8, offset)
        chunks.append(entry_data)
        offset += len(entry_data)
        centrals.append(cen["central"])

    central_dir = b"".join(centrals)
    cd_offset = offset
    cd_size = len(central_dir)

    out = b"".join(chunks) + central_dir

    # Determine whether we need ZIP64 structures (if any central size/offset or file count exceeds 0xFFFF/0xFFFFFFFF)
    total_entries = len(files)
    need_zip64 = cd_offset >= 0xFFFFFFFF or cd_size >= 0xFFFFFFFF or total_entries >= 0xFFFF

    if need_zip64:
        # ZIP64 end of central directory record
        zip64_eocd = struct.pack(
            "<IQHHIIQQQQ",
            ZIP64_END_CENTRAL_DIR_SIG,
            44,             # size of remaining record
            45,             # version made by
            45,             # version needed
            0,              # disk number
            0,              # disk with central dir
            total_entries,
            total_entries,
            cd_size,
            cd_offset,
        )
        out += zip64_eocd
        # ZIP64 end of central directory locator
        zip64_locator = struct.pack(
            "<IIQI",
            ZIP64_END_CENTRAL_DIR_LOC_SIG,
            0,
            cd_offset + cd_size,  # relative offset of zip64 eocd
            1
        )
        out += zip64_locator

    # Traditional EOCD (with truncation if zip64 is used)
    comment = b""
    out += struct.pack(
        "<IHHHHIIH",
        END_CENTRAL_DIR_SIG,
        0,
        0,
        min(total_entries, 0xFFFF),
        min(total_entries, 0xFFFF),
        min(cd_size, 0xFFFFFFFF),
        min(cd_offset, 0xFFFFFFFF),
        len(comment)
    ) + comment

    return out


def _random_content(rnd: random.Random, name: str) -> bytes:
    # Generate diverse contents based on extension
    ext = name.rstrip('/').split('.')[-1] if '.' in name.rstrip('/') else ''
    if name.endswith('/'):
        return b""  # directories have no data
    if ext.lower() in ("txt", "ini"):
        lines = []
        for _ in range(rnd.randint(3, 20)):
            line = ''.join(rnd.choice("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 -_:/\\") for _ in range(rnd.randint(5, 60)))
            lines.append(line)
        return ('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode('utf-8')
    if ext.lower() == "png":
        # Minimal PNG-like header + random bytes to be plausible
        sig = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
        data = rnd.randbytes(rnd.randint(16, 128))
        return sig + data
    if ext.lower() == "bin":
        return rnd.randbytes(rnd.randint(32, 256))
    if ext.lower() == "exec":
        return b"#!/bin/sh\necho hello\n"
    # default
    return rnd.randbytes(rnd.randint(0, 200))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide number of entries: 1..6 to keep under 4096 bytes
    n = rnd.randint(1, 6)
    names = []
    for _ in range(n):
        # Ensure unique names to avoid duplicates
        for _attempt in range(10):
            nm = _rand_filename(rnd)
            if nm not in names:
                names.append(nm)
                break
        else:
            names.append(f"file{len(names)}.txt")

    files = []

    # Choose a strategy mix: include stored and deflated, with/without data descriptor, UTF-8, and possibly a directory
    for i, name in enumerate(names):
        utf8 = any(ord(c) > 127 for c in name)
        method = rnd.choice([STORE, DEFLATE])
        use_descriptor = rnd.random() < 0.4
        content = _random_content(rnd, name)

        # Occasionally force ZIP64 sizes by faking descriptor sizes? Instead, emulate large by toggling flag and ensuring ZIP64 in central via offset later when needed.
        # To remain valid and small, we do not actually need ZIP64 unless we set flags in central. We'll add one entry with ZIP64 fields by pretending offset needs ZIP64: place it after a large padding dummy if chosen.
        force_zip64_sizes = False
        files.append((name, content, method, use_descriptor, force_zip64_sizes, utf8))

    # Optionally add a directory entry if not present
    if not any(n.endswith('/') for n in names) and rnd.random() < 0.5 and len(files) < 6:
        dir_name = "dir_{}/".format(rnd.randint(1, 999))
        files.insert(0, (dir_name, b"", STORE, False, False, False))

    # Build archive initially
    data = _build_archive(rnd, files)

    # Keep under 4096 bytes; if over, reduce by removing some files
    while len(data) > 4096 and len(files) > 1:
        files.pop()
        data = _build_archive(rnd, files)

    # With small probability, build an archive that uses data descriptors for all file entries
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        files2 = []
        for (name, content, method, _, fz, utf8) in files:
            files2.append((name, content, method, True, fz, utf8))
        data2 = _build_archive(rnd, files2)
        if len(data2) <= 4096:
            data = data2

    return data

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target data type: opaque filename pointer passed to fopen-like backends.
# In these stubs, FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() will materialize a temporary file
# whose contents come from our returned bytes. The backend is the standard
# fill_fopen_filefunc/fopen64, so it expects a C string path to a real file.
# Therefore, to exercise open/seek/tell paths meaningfully, we should return
# bytes that form valid file contents. fopen modes are fuzzed by the harness;
# we cannot influence them directly, but providing content that is valid for
# both text and binary reads and of varying sizes allows seeks and tells to
# succeed across origins (SET/CUR/END).
#
# Strategy:
# - Generate a small to moderate file (0..~3KB) with structured content so
#   seek/tell over different offsets is meaningful.
# - Ensure the content is valid for both text and binary interpretations:
#   * Mix of ASCII text lines with newlines (for text mode)
#   * Binary blocks with zero bytes and high-bit bytes (for binary mode)
# - Include recognizable headers like "PK\x03\x04" (ZIP local header) and
#   "PK\x05\x06" (End of central directory) at varying positions to touch
#   potential optimizations in some backends, but the stubs only open/seek/tell.
# - Include NUL bytes so that if any buggy code mistakenly treats the file
#   content pointer as a C-string, it might stop early while still being valid.
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# The returned bytes become the file content that the harness writes for the
# filename it passes to the callbacks.

ASCII_WORDS: List[str] = [
    "alpha", "bravo", "charlie", "delta", "echo", "foxtrot",
    "golf", "hotel", "india", "juliet", "kilo", "lima",
    "mike", "november", "oscar", "papa", "quebec", "romeo",
    "sierra", "tango", "uniform", "victor", "whiskey", "xray",
    "yankee", "zulu"
]

def _rand_ascii_line(rng: random.Random, min_words=3, max_words=12) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_words, max_words)
    words = rng.sample(ASCII_WORDS, k=min(n, len(ASCII_WORDS)))
    # Randomly change case to exercise case handling in potential paths
    out = []
    for w in words:
        mode = rng.randint(0, 2)
        if mode == 0:
            out.append(w.lower())
        elif mode == 1:
            out.append(w.upper())
        else:
            out.append(w.capitalize())
    line = " ".join(out)
    # Occasionally include a UTF-8 character while staying valid text
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        line += " – café naïve résumé"
    return (line + "\n").encode("utf-8")

def _binary_block(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    # Create structured binary with repeating patterns and some randomness
    parts = []
    # Header marker block
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(b"PK\x03\x04")  # ZIP local header signature
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        parts.append(b"PK\x05\x06")  # End of central directory
    # Add a NUL run
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        parts.append(b"\x00" * rng.randint(4, 32))
    # Add increasing byte sequence
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        seq_len = rng.randint(8, 64)
        parts.append(bytes((i % 256 for i in range(seq_len))))
    # Add random bytes
    rand_len = max(0, size - sum(len(p) for p in parts))
    parts.append(rng.randbytes(rand_len))
    return b"".join(parts)[:size]

def _make_content(rng: random.Random, target_size: int) -> bytes:
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    # File preamble: magic, version, and a small header
    magic = b"FILE\x00"
    version = struct.pack("<H", rng.randint(1, 0xFFFF))
    flags = struct.pack("<I", rng.getrandbits(32))
    chunks.append(magic + version + flags)

    # A few text lines
    n_lines = rng.randint(3, 20)
    for _ in range(n_lines):
        line = _rand_ascii_line(rng)
        chunks.append(line)

    # Insert a binary block
    bin_size = rng.randint(32, 512)
    chunks.append(_binary_block(rng, bin_size))

    # Another set of lines including long one
    long_line = ("L" * rng.randint(64, 512)) + "\n"
    chunks.append(long_line.encode("utf-8"))

    # Footer with sizes
    body = b"".join(chunks)
    # Add an index-like footer containing offsets to a couple of markers
    markers = [b"alpha", b"PK\x03\x04", b"\n"]
    footer = bytearray()
    footer += b"IDX0"
    for m in markers:
        pos = body.find(m)
        footer += struct.pack("<q", pos)  # -1 if not found
    footer += b"END0"

    content = body + footer

    # Adjust to target size with padding or truncation
    if len(content) < target_size:
        pad_needed = target_size - len(content)
        # pad with a mix of zeros and random bytes
        pad_zeros = min(pad_needed, rng.randint(0, pad_needed))
        padding = b"\x00" * pad_zeros + rng.randbytes(pad_needed - pad_zeros)
        content += padding
    else:
        content = content[:target_size]

    return content

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a total size up to 3.5 KiB to allow room yet stay < 4096
    total_size = rng.randint(0, 3584)

    # Occasionally generate empty files to test edge cases (open succeeds, size 0)
    if rng.random() < 0.05:
        return b""

    # Bias towards having at least some content to make seek/tell meaningful
    min_size = 64
    total_size = max(total_size, min_size)

    content = _make_content(rng, total_size)

    # Ensure trailing newline sometimes, to be friendly for text mode
    if rng.random() < 0.5 and (len(content) == 0 or content[-1] != 0x0A):
        # Only append if it won't exceed 4096
        if len(content) + 1 <= 4096:
            content += b"\n"
        else:
            content = content[:-1] + b"\n"

    # Final clamp to 4096 bytes
    return content[:4096]
